I'm a 65-year-old man farming these 7.7 mu in Dongmaliangu village, Anzhai township. I've been at this for 45 years — my father handed me the hoe when I was 20, and I've worked this land ever since. I only went to primary school, so I don't read much, but I know my fields. My wife and I do most of the work. Our son is off in the city working construction, so he only comes back for wheat harvest and to help pick cotton in the fall. We have 4.7 mu in the wheat-maize rotation and 3 mu in cotton. That's how we've always done it — the wheat-maize gives us grain and steady income, and cotton pays a bit better when the price is right, though it's hard on these old bones.

**Wheat:** The wheat went in last October 10th, same as every year. I used about 7–8 jin of seed per mu, bought from the seed station for about 15 yuan per mu. I don't save my own wheat seed anymore — the bought seed sprouts better. For fertilizer, I put down about 40–45 kg of compound per mu at planting — the kind with 18-25-5 on the bag. That cost me about 55 yuan per mu. Then at green-up time in March I topdressed with another 20 kg or so of compound, and I just put down about 4–5 kg of urea per mu at jointing now that it's April. The wheat is looking decent, not great — last year I got about 550 kg per mu, and if the weather holds I might get close to that again. I'll irrigate three times: the green-up water, one at jointing, and one when the grain is filling. Each irrigation costs about 10–12 yuan per mu in electricity for the pump. I sprayed insecticide twice already for aphids, and I'll watch for rust. Harvest will be around June 5th — I hire the combine, costs about 10 yuan per mu. I do the cutting and hauling myself.

**Summer maize:** As soon as the wheat is off — usually by June 10th — I plant the maize. The window is tight, maybe 5–6 days. I hire the tractor to rotary till, then I plant Denghai 605, about 1.2 packages per mu, costs around 14 yuan per mu. I don't till much myself anymore — my back can't take it. For fertilizer, I put about 35 kg of compound per mu at planting — the 28-6-6 kind. That's about 45 yuan per mu. No topdressing usually — by the time the maize needs it, I'm busy with cotton and the rain sometimes comes. I irrigate two or three times, depending on the rain. Last year I got about 600 kg per mu. I hope for the same. Harvest is mid-October.

**Cotton:** I plant the cotton around April 19th–20th, right about now. I use about 2.5 jin of seed per mu, costs about 15 yuan per mu. I rotary till first — 50 yuan for the tractor for the whole plot. I put down about 50 kg of compound per mu at planting — the 20-10-21 kind, costs about 70 yuan per mu. Cotton is hungry work. I irrigate three times: once at flowering, once at boll stage, and once more if it's dry. Water costs about 15 yuan per mu each time. The real cost is pesticide — I spray insecticide 15–17 times through the season for bollworm. That costs me over 100 yuan for the 3 mu. I also spray herbicide once and do hand-weeding. Cotton needs pruning too — my wife and I spend many days on that. Yield last year was about 260 kg per mu of seed cotton. I hope for the same, but the price is always a gamble.

**Money and labor:** I'm cash-tight. Every yuan I spend on fertilizer is a yuan I don't have for medicine or repairs. I could put more fertilizer on, but I've learned that after a point it doesn't pay back. My neighbor Wang put on 50 kg more compound per mu last year and only got 20 kg more wheat — not worth it. I hire labor only when I must: combine for wheat, maybe a bit of picking help for cotton. Family labor is 4 of us, but only my wife and I are here full-time. My son sends money back, which helps, but I don't count on it for farm inputs.

**Why I do it this way:** I've tried changing things — new varieties, different fertilizer — but the old way works. Wheat-maize gives me two crops and spreads the risk. Cotton is extra cash, but if the bollworm is bad, I lose. I plant what I know, spend what I can afford, and keep some cash in my pocket for when the pump breaks or I need to see the doctor. At my age, I'm not experimenting anymore. I want steady, not spectacular.
